metadata.name: Electronic Navigational Chart
metadata.scope: Ocean, Coastal, Ports and Harbors. Excludes Inland waters.

features.name: Quality of Non-Bathymetric Data
features.definition: An area within which a uniform assessment of the quality of the non-bathymetric data exists.

features.name: Data Coverage
features.definition: A geographical area that describes the coverage and extent of spatial objects.

features.name: Navigational System of Marks
features.definition: An area within which the navigational system of marks has been established in relation to a specific direction.

features.name: Local Direction of Buoyage
features.definition: An area within which the navigational system of marks has been established in relation to a specific direction.

features.name: Quality of Bathymetric Data
features.definition: An area within which a uniform assessment of the quality of the bathymetric data exists.

features.name: Sounding Datum
features.definition: The horizontal plane or tidal datum to which soundings have been reduced. Also called datum for sounding reduction.

features.name: Vertical Datum of Data
features.definition: Any level surface (for example Mean Sea Level) taken as a surface of reference to which the elevations within a data set are reduced. Also called datum level, reference level, reference plane, levelling datum, datum for heights.

features.name: Quality of Survey
features.definition: An area within which a uniform assessment of the reliability of source survey information exists.

features.name: Update Information
features.definition: The Update Information metadata feature is used to represent a change to the information shown.

features.name: Magnetic Variation
features.definition: The angle between the magnetic and geographic meridians at any place, expressed in degrees east or west to indicate the direction of magnetic north from true north. Also called magnetic declination.

features.name: Local Magnetic Anomaly
features.definition: An anomaly of the magnetic field of the Earth, extending over a relatively small area, due to local magnetic influences. Also called local attraction or magnetic anomaly.

features.name: Coastline
features.definition: The line where shore and water meet. Shoreline and coastline are generally used synonymously.

features.name: Land Area
features.definition: The solid portion of the Earth's surface, as opposed to sea, water.

features.name: Island Group
features.definition: A named group of islands, including archipelagos.

features.name: Land Elevation
features.definition: An elevation is the vertical distance of a point or a level, on, or affixed to, the surface of the earth, measured from a specified vertical datum.

features.name: River
features.definition: A relatively large natural stream of water.

features.name: Rapids
features.definition: Portions of a stream with accelerated current where it descends rapidly but without a break in the slope of the bed sufficient to form a waterfall. Usually used in the plural.

features.name: Waterfall
features.definition: A vertically descending part of a watercourse where it falls from a height (for example: over a rock or a precipice). In place names, commonly shortened to fall or falls, for example Niagara Falls.

features.name: Lake
features.definition: A large body of water entirely surrounded by land.

features.name: Land Region
features.definition: An area of natural or cultivated scenery defined by its geographical characteristics and may be known by its proper name.

features.name: Vegetation
features.definition: Plants collectively or individually, especially those dominating a particular area or habitat.

features.name: Ice Area
features.definition: An area of ice over land or water.

features.name: Sloping Ground
features.definition: An inclined surface.

features.name: Slope Topline
features.definition: The upper marking of a slope, for example the ridge line or the separation line between two different gradients.

features.name: Tideway
features.definition: A channel through which a tidal current runs.

features.name: Built-Up Area
features.definition: An area of land or construction over the water containing a concentration of buildings and/or other structures.

features.name: Building
features.definition: A free-standing self-supporting construction that is roofed, usually walled, and is intended for human occupancy (for example: a place of work or recreation) and/or habitation.

features.name: Airport/Airfield
features.definition: A defined area on land (including any buildings, installations and equipment) intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircraft.

features.name: Runway
features.definition: A defined area, on a land aerodrome, prepared for the landing and take-off run of aircraft.

features.name: Helipad
features.definition: A site on which helicopters may land and take off.

features.name: Bridge
features.definition: A structure erected over a depression or an obstacle such as a body of water, railroad, etc., to provide a roadway for vehicles or pedestrians.

features.name: Span Fixed
features.definition: A fixed component of the deck of a bridge spanning successive bridge piers.

features.name: Span Opening
features.definition: An opening component of the deck of a bridge spanning successive bridge piers.

features.name: Conveyor
features.definition: A mechanical device for conveying bulk material or people using an endless moving belt or series of rollers.

features.name: Cable Overhead
features.definition: A single continuous rope-like bundle consisting of multiple strands of fiber, plastic, metal, and/or glass, which is supported by structures such as poles or pylons and passing over or nearby navigable waters.

features.name: Pipeline Overhead
features.definition: A string of interconnected pipes, supported by pylons and passing over or nearby navigable waters, used for the transport of matter, nowadays mainly oil or gas.

features.name: Pylon/Bridge Support
features.definition: A vertical construction consisting, for example, of a steel framework or pre-stressed concrete to carry cables, a bridge, etc.

features.name: Fence/Wall
features.definition: A man-made barrier used as an enclosure or boundary or for protection.

features.name: Railway
features.definition: A rail or set of parallel rails on which a train, tram, or rail wagon runs.

features.name: Road
features.definition: A route with a specially prepared surface that is intended for use by wheeled vehicles or pedestrians.

features.name: Tunnel
features.definition: A passage that is open to the atmosphere at both ends, buried under the seabed or laid over the seafloor or bored under the ground or through mountains.

features.name: Landmark
features.definition: Any prominent object at a fixed location on land which can be used in determining a location or a direction.

features.name: Silo/Tank
features.definition: A large storage structure used for storing loose materials, liquids and/or gases.

features.name: Wind Turbine
features.definition: A tower and associated equipment that generates electrical power from wind. They can be sited offshore and may be either fixed or floating.

features.name: Fortified Structure
features.definition: A structure that is specifically designed or reinforced to provide for defence from armed attack.

features.name: Production/Storage Area
features.definition: An area on land for the exploitation or storage of natural resources.

features.name: Checkpoint
features.definition: An official location at which to register, declare and/or inspect goods and/or people.

features.name: Hulk
features.definition: The hull of a wrecked or condemned ship, from which the fittings and superstructure have usually been removed, which is moored in a permanent position or grounded. It may be abandoned or put to some other use.

features.name: Pile
features.definition: A long heavy timber or section of steel, wood, concrete, etc., forced into the earth or seafloor to serve as a support, as for a pier, or to resist lateral pressure; or as a free standing pole within a marine environment.

features.name: Dyke
features.definition: A dyke (or dike) is an artificial embankment to contain or hold back water.

features.name: Shoreline Construction
features.definition: A fixed artificial structure in the water and/or adjoining the land. It may also refer to features such as training walls, which are not necessarily connected to, nor form part of the shoreline.

features.name: Structure Over Navigable Water
features.definition: A roofed structure erected, or partly erected, over a body of water, to provide protection for a vessel or its cargo.

features.name: Causeway
features.definition: A raised way across low or wet ground or water.

features.name: Canal
features.definition: An artificial waterway with no flow, or a controlled flow, used for navigation, or for draining or irrigating land (ditch).

features.name: Distance Mark
features.definition: A distance mark indicates the distance measured from an origin and consists of either a solid visible structure or a distinct location without special installation. Usually found on canals.

features.name: Gate
features.definition: A structure that may be swung, drawn, or lowered to block an entrance or passageway on a watercourse.

features.name: Dam
features.definition: A barrier to check or confine anything in motion; particularly one constructed to hold back water and raise its level to form a reservoir, or to prevent flooding.

features.name: Crane
features.definition: A machine for lifting, shifting and lowering objects or materials by means of a swinging boom or with a lifting apparatus supported on an overhead track.

features.name: Berth
features.definition: A place, generally named or numbered, where a vessel may moor or anchor.

features.name: Dolphin
features.definition: A post or group of posts, used for mooring or warping a vessel, or as an aid to navigation. The dolphin may be in the water, on a wharf or on the beach.

features.name: Bollard
features.definition: Small shaped post, mounted on a wharf or dolphin used to secure ship's lines.

features.name: Dry Dock
features.definition: An artificial basin fitted with a gate or caisson, into which vessels can be floated and the water pumped out to expose the vessel's bottom. Also called graving dock.

features.name: Floating Dock
features.definition: A form of dry dock consisting of a floating structure of one or more sections which can be partly submerged by controlled flooding to receive a vessel, then raised by pumping out the water so that the vessel's bottom can be exposed.

features.name: Pontoon
features.definition: A floating structure, usually rectangular in shape which serves as landing, pier head, bridge support, etc.

features.name: Dock Area
features.definition: An artificially enclosed area within which ships may moor and which may have gates to regulate water level.

features.name: Gridiron
features.definition: A structure in the intertidal zone serving as a support for vessels at low stages of the tide to permit work on the exposed portion of the vessel's hull.

features.name: Lock Basin
features.definition: A wet dock in a waterway, permitting a ship to pass from one level to another.

features.name: Mooring Trot
features.definition: A mooring is a place where a vessel may be secured. A mooring trot is a mooring that is composed of ground tackle, mooring cables, buoys and mooring berths on junction cables.

features.name: Sea Area/Named Water Area
features.definition: A geographically defined part of the sea or other navigable waters. It may be specified within its limits by its proper name.

features.name: Tidal Stream - Flood/Ebb
features.definition: Approximate tidal stream rates given as discrete rate values for flood and ebb flow during springs.

features.name: Current - Non-Gravitational
features.definition: Any current that is caused by other than tide producing forces.

features.name: Water Turbulence
features.definition: The disturbance of water caused by the interaction of any combination of waves, currents, tidal streams, wind, shoal patches and obstructions.

features.name: Tidal Stream Panel Data
features.definition: Approximate tidal stream characteristics given as discrete value sets at a specified interval before and/or after a high or low water.

features.name: Sounding
features.definition: Measured or charted depth of water (may be a drying height), or the measurement of such a depth, which has been reduced to a vertical datum.

features.name: Dredged Area
features.definition: An area of the bottom of a body of water which has been deepened by dredging.

features.name: Swept Area
features.definition: An area that has been determined to be clear of navigational dangers to a specified depth.

features.name: Depth Contour
features.definition: A line connecting points of equal water depth which is sometimes significantly displaced outside of soundings, symbols, and other chart detail for clarity as well as generalization. Depth contours therefore often represent an approximate location of the line of equal depth as related to the surveyed line delineated on the source.

features.name: Depth Area
features.definition: A water area whose depth is within a defined range of values.

features.name: Depth - No Bottom Found
features.definition: Upon investigation the bottom was not found at this depth.

features.name: Unsurveyed Area
features.definition: An area where hydrographic survey data is non-existent.

features.name: Seabed Area
features.definition: A region of the seabed including the material of which it is composed and its physical characteristics. Also called nature of bottom, character (or characteristics) of the bottom, or quality of the bottom.

features.name: Weed/Kelp
features.definition: Any macroscopic marine alga.

features.name: Seagrass
features.definition: Any of various submerged monocotyledonous plants (such as eelgrass, tape grass, and turtle grass) of tropical to temperate usually shallow coastal waters that have narrow grass-like leaves and often form dense underwater meadows.

features.name: Sandwave
features.definition: Large mobile wave-like sediment feature in shallow water and composed of sand. The wavelength may reach 100 metres, the amplitude may be up to 20 metres.

features.name: Spring
features.definition: A natural issue of water or other substances from the earth. One on the bottom of the sea is called a submarine spring.

features.name: Underwater/Awash Rock
features.definition: A concreted mass of stony material or coral which dries, is awash or is below the water surface.

features.name: Wreck
features.definition: The ruined remains of a stranded or sunken vessel which has been rendered useless.

features.name: Obstruction
features.definition: In marine navigation, anything that hinders or prevents movement, particularly anything that endangers or prevents passage of a vessel. The term is usually used to refer to an isolated danger to navigation, such as a sunken rock or pinnacle.

features.name: Foul Ground
features.definition: Areas over which it is safe to navigate but which should be avoided for anchoring, taking the ground or ground fishing.

features.name: Discoloured Water
features.definition: Unnatural coloured areas in the sea which may or may not indicate the existence of shoals.

features.name: Fishing Facility
features.definition: A structure for fishing purposes which can be an obstruction to ships in general. The position of these structures may vary frequently over time.

features.name: Marine Farm/Culture
features.definition: An assemblage of cages, nets, rafts and floats or posts where fish, including shellfish, are artificially cultivated.

features.name: Offshore Platform
features.definition: A permanent offshore structure, either fixed or floating.

features.name: Cable Submarine
features.definition: An assembly of wires or fibres, or a wire rope or chain, which has been laid underwater or buried beneath the seafloor.

features.name: Cable Area
features.definition: An area which contains one or more submarine cables.

features.name: Pipeline Submarine/On Land
features.definition: A connected set of pipes for conveying liquids, slurries, or gases.

features.name: Submarine Pipeline Area
features.definition: An area containing one or more submarine pipelines.

features.name: Offshore Production Area
features.definition: An area at sea within which there are production facilities.

features.name: Navigation Line
features.definition: A straight line extending towards an area of navigational interest and generally generated by two navigational aids or one navigational aid and a bearing.

features.name: Recommended Track
features.definition: A route which has been specially examined to ensure so far as possible that it is free of dangers and along which ships are advised to navigate.

features.name: Range System
features.definition: Two or more features in the same horizontal direction, particularly those features so placed as navigational aids to mark any line of importance to vessels, as a channel. The one nearest the observer is the front mark and the one farthest from the observer is the rear mark.

features.name: Fairway
features.definition: That part of a river, harbour and so on, where the main navigable channel for vessels of larger size lies. It is also the usual course followed by vessels entering or leaving harbours, called 'ship channel'.

features.name: Fairway System
features.definition: That part of a river, harbour and so on, where the main navigable channel for vessels of larger size lies. It is also the usual course followed by vessels entering or leaving harbours, called 'ship channel'. A fairway system is an aggregation of connected fairway features making up a complex fairway system.

features.name: Recommended Route Centreline
features.definition: The recommended route centreline indicates the 'centreline' of a recommended route.

features.name: Two-Way Route Part
features.definition: An area of a two-way route within which traffic flow is generally along one bearing (and possibly its reciprocal).

features.name: Two-Way Route
features.definition: A route within defined limits inside which two way traffic is established, aimed at providing safe passage of ships through waters where navigation is difficult or dangerous.

features.name: Recommended Traffic Lane Part
features.definition: A traffic flow pattern indicating a recommended directional movement of traffic where it is impractical or unnecessary to adopt an established direction of traffic flow.

features.name: Deep Water Route Centreline
features.definition: The Deep Water route centreline indicates the centreline of a route, the width of which is not explicitly defined.

features.name: Deep Water Route Part
features.definition: An area of a deep water route within which ships proceed in the same direction.

features.name: Deep Water Route
features.definition: A route within defined limits which has been accurately surveyed for clearance of sea bottom and submerged obstacles as indicated on the chart.

features.name: Inshore Traffic Zone
features.definition: A routeing measure comprising a designated area between the landward boundary of a traffic separation scheme and the adjacent coast, to be used in accordance with the provisions of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.

features.name: Precautionary Area
features.definition: A routeing measure comprising an area within defined limits where ships must navigate with particular caution and within which the direction of traffic flow may be recommended.

features.name: Traffic Separation Scheme Lane Part
features.definition: An area within defined limits in which one-way traffic is established. Natural obstacles, including those forming separation zones, may constitute a boundary.

features.name: Separation Zone or Line
features.definition: A zone or line separating the traffic lanes in which ships are proceeding in opposite, or nearly opposite directions; or separating a traffic lane from the adjacent sea area; or separating traffic lanes designated for particular classes of ships proceeding in the same direction.

features.name: Traffic Separation Scheme Boundary
features.definition: The outer limit of a traffic lane part or a traffic separation scheme roundabout.

features.name: Traffic Separation Scheme Crossing
features.definition: A defined area where traffic lanes cross.

features.name: Traffic Separation Scheme Roundabout
features.definition: A routeing measure comprising a separation point or circular separation zone and a circular traffic lane within defined limits. Traffic within the roundabout is separated by moving in a counter-clockwise direction around the separation point or zone.

features.name: Traffic Separation Scheme
features.definition: A routeing measure aimed at the separation of opposing streams of traffic by appropriate means and by the establishment of traffic lanes.

features.name: Archipelagic Sea Lane Area
features.definition: Sea lanes designated by an archipelagic State for the passage of ships and aircraft.

features.name: Archipelagic Sea Lane Axis
features.definition: The reference line used to determine the maximum extents of an Archipelagic Sea Lane. It may not indicate the deepest water nor any recommended route or track.

features.name: Archipelagic Sea Lane
features.definition: Sea lanes designated by an archipelagic State for the passage of ships and aircraft. The Archipelagic Sea Lane aggregates all component parts of an Archipelagic Sea Lane system.

features.name: Radio Calling-In Point
features.definition: A designated position at which vessels are required to report to a traffic control centre. Also called reporting point or radio reporting point.

features.name: Ferry Route
features.definition: A route in a body of water where a ferry crosses from one shoreline to another.

features.name: Radar Line
features.definition: Recommended tracks along which ships can be guided by coastal radar stations in the event of bad visibility.

features.name: Radar Range
features.definition: Indicates the coverage of a sea area by a radar surveillance station. Inside this area a vessel may request shore-based radar assistance, particularly in poor visibility.

features.name: Radar Station
features.definition: A station with a transmitter emitting pulses of ultra-high frequency radio waves which are reflected by solid objects and are detected upon their return to the sending station.

features.name: Anchorage Area
features.definition: An area in which vessels or seaplanes anchor or may anchor.

features.name: Mooring Area
features.definition: An area in which vessels may be secured to mooring buoys

features.name: Anchor Berth
features.definition: A designated area of water where a vessel, seaplane, etc., may anchor.

features.name: Seaplane Landing Area
features.definition: A designated portion of water for the landing and take-off of seaplanes.

features.name: Dumping Ground
features.definition: A sea area where dredged material or other potentially more harmful material, for example explosives, chemical waste, is deliberately deposited.

features.name: Military Practice Area
features.definition: An area within which naval, military or aerial exercises are carried out.

features.name: Administration Area
features.definition: A defined area within which a jurisdiction applies. It may or may not be named.

features.name: Cargo Transhipment Area
features.definition: An area designated for transfer of cargo from one vessel to another sometimes in order to reduce a vessel's draught.

features.name: Caution Area
features.definition: Generally, an area where the mariner has to be made aware of circumstances influencing the safety of navigation.

features.name: Information Area
features.definition: An area for which general information regarding navigation, but not directly related to safety of navigation, is available.

features.name: Contiguous Zone
features.definition: A zone contiguous to a coastal State's Territorial Sea, which may not extend beyond 24 nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of the Territorial Sea is measured. The coastal State may exercise certain control in this zone subject to the provisions of International Law.

features.name: Continental Shelf Area
features.definition: The Continental Shelf of a coastal State comprises the seabed and subsoil of the submarine areas that extend beyond its Territorial Sea throughout the natural prolongation of its land territory to the outer edge of the continental margin, or to a distance of 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of the Territorial Sea is measured where the outer edge of the continental margin does not extend up to that distance.

features.name: Custom Zone
features.definition: The area within which national custom regulations are in force.

features.name: Exclusive Economic Zone
features.definition: An area, not exceeding 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of the territorial sea is measured, subject to a specific legal regime established in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea under which the coastal state has certain rights and jurisdiction.

features.name: Fishery Zone
features.definition: The offshore zone in which exclusive fishing rights and management are held by the coastal nation.

features.name: Fishing Ground
features.definition: A water area in which fishing is frequently carried on.

features.name: Free Port Area
features.definition: A port where certain import and export duties are waived (unless goods pass into the country) to facilitate reshipment to other countries.

features.name: Harbour Area (Administrative)
features.definition: The area over which a harbour authority has jurisdiction.

features.name: Log Pond
features.definition: A maritime area enclosed with connected floating timbers used as a staging area for sawn logs.

features.name: Oil Barrier
features.definition: A floating barrier to stop and contain the spread of oil on a water body surface.

features.name: Straight Territorial Sea Baseline
features.definition: Straight baselines are a system of straight lines joining specified or discrete points on the low-water line, usually known as straight baseline turning points. Straight baselines are used in delimitation.

features.name: Territorial Sea Area
features.definition: A belt of water of a defined breadth but not exceeding 12 nautical miles measured seaward from the territorial sea baseline.

features.name: Submarine Transit Lane
features.definition: A lane where submarines may navigate under water or at the surface.

features.name: Pilotage District
features.definition: An area within which a pilotage direction exists. Such directions are regulated by a competent harbour authority which dictates circumstances under which they apply.

features.name: Collision Regulations Limit
features.definition: Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972 (COLREGs). The demarcation line between inland navigation rules and international navigation rules.

features.name: Marine Pollution Regulations Area
features.definition: The International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL) is the main international convention covering prevention of pollution of the marine environment by ships from operational or accidental causes.

features.name: Restricted Area
features.definition: A specified area on land or water designated by an appropriate authority within which access or navigation is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

features.name: Light All Around
features.definition: An all around light is a light that is visible over the whole horizon of interest to marine navigation and having no change in the characteristics of the light.

features.name: Light Sectored
features.definition: A light presenting different appearances (in particular, different colours) over various parts of the horizon of interest to maritime navigation.

features.name: Light Fog Detector
features.definition: A fog detector light is a light used to automatically determine conditions of visibility which warrant the turning on or off of a sound signal.

features.name: Light Air Obstruction
features.definition: An air obstruction light is a light marking an obstacle which constitutes a danger to air navigation.

features.name: Lateral Buoy
features.definition: A lateral buoy is used to indicate the port or starboard hand side of the route to be followed. They are generally used for well-defined channels and are used in conjunction with a conventional direction of buoyage.

features.name: Cardinal Buoy
features.definition: A cardinal buoy is used in conjunction with the compass to indicate where the mariner may find the best navigable water. It is placed in one of the four quadrants (North, East, South and West), bounded by inter-cardinal bearings from the point marked.

features.name: Isolated Danger Buoy
features.definition: An isolated danger buoy is a buoy moored on or above an isolated danger of limited extent, which has navigable water all around it.

features.name: Safe Water Buoy
features.definition: A safe water buoy is used to indicate that there is navigable water around the mark.

features.name: Special Purpose/General Buoy
features.definition: A special purpose buoy is primarily used to indicate an area or feature, the nature of which is apparent from reference to a chart, Sailing Directions or Notices to Mariners.

features.name: Emergency Wreck Marking Buoy
features.definition: An emergency wreck marking buoy is a buoy moored on or above a new wreck, designed to provide a prominent (both visual and radio) and easily identifiable temporary first response.

features.name: Installation Buoy
features.definition: An installation buoy is a buoy used for loading tankers with gas or oil.

features.name: Mooring Buoy
features.definition: A buoy secured to the bottom by permanent moorings with means for mooring a vessel by use of its anchor chain or mooring lines.

features.name: Lateral Beacon
features.definition: A lateral beacon is used to indicate the port or starboard hand side of the route to be followed. They are generally used for well defined channels and are used in conjunction with a conventional direction of buoyage.

features.name: Cardinal Beacon
features.definition: A cardinal beacon is used in conjunction with the compass to indicate where the mariner may find the best navigable water. It is placed in one of the four quadrants (North, East, South and West), bounded by inter-cardinal bearings from the point marked.

features.name: Isolated Danger Beacon
features.definition: An isolated danger beacon is a beacon erected on an isolated danger of limited extent, which has navigable water all around it.

features.name: Safe Water Beacon
features.definition: A safe water beacon is used to indicate that there is navigable water around the mark.

features.name: Special Purpose/General Beacon
features.definition: A special purpose beacon is primarily used to indicate an area or feature, the nature of which is apparent from reference to a chart, Sailing Directions or Notices to Mariners.

features.name: Daymark
features.definition: The identifying characteristics of an aid to navigation which serve to facilitate its recognition against a daylight viewing background. On those structures that do not by themselves present an adequate viewing area to be seen at the required distance, the aid is made more visible by affixing a daymark to the structure. A daymark so affixed has a distinctive colour and shape depending on the purpose of the aid.

features.name: Light Float
features.definition: A boat-like structure used instead of a light buoy in waters where strong streams or currents are experienced, or when a greater elevation than that of a light buoy is necessary.

features.name: Light Vessel
features.definition: A distinctively marked vessel anchored or moored at a charted point, to serve as an aid to navigation. By night, it displays a characteristic light(s) and is usually equipped with other devices, such as fog signal, submarine sound signal, and radio-beacon, to assist navigation.

features.name: Retroreflector
features.definition: A means of distinguishing unlighted marks at night. Retroreflective material is secured to the mark in a particular pattern to reflect back light.

features.name: Radar Reflector
features.definition: A device capable of, or intended for, reflecting radar signals.

features.name: Fog Signal
features.definition: A warning signal transmitted by a vessel, or aid to navigation, during periods of low visibility. Also, the device producing such a signal.

features.name: Physical AIS Aid to Navigation
features.definition: An Automatic Identification System (AIS) message 21 transmitted from a physical Aid to Navigation, or transmitted from an AIS station for an Aid to Navigation which physically exists.

features.name: Virtual AIS Aid to Navigation
features.definition: An Automatic Identification System (AIS) message 21 transmitted from an AIS station to simulate on navigation systems an Aid to Navigation which does not physically exist.

features.name: Radio Station
features.definition: A place equipped to transmit radio waves. Such a station may be either stationary or mobile, and may also be provided with a radio receiver.

features.name: Radar Transponder Beacon
features.definition: A transponder beacon transmitting a coded signal on radar frequency, permitting an interrogating craft to determine the bearing and range of the transponder.

features.name: Pilot Boarding Place
features.definition: A location offshore where a pilot may board a vessel in preparation to piloting it through local waters.

features.name: Vessel Traffic Service Area
features.definition: The area of any service implemented by a relevant authority primarily designed to improve safety and efficiency of traffic flow and the protection of the environment. It may range from simple information messages, to extensive organisation of the traffic involving national or regional schemes.

features.name: Coast Guard Station
features.definition: A station at which a visual/radio/radar marine watch is kept either continuously or at certain times only.

features.name: Signal Station Warning
features.definition: A warning signal station is a place on shore from which warning signals are made to ships at sea.

features.name: Signal Station Traffic
features.definition: A traffic signal station is a place on shore from which signals are made to regulate the movement of traffic.

features.name: Rescue Station
features.definition: A place where equipment for saving life at sea is maintained.

features.name: Harbour Facility
features.definition: A harbour installation with a service or commercial operation of public interest.

features.name: Small Craft Facility
features.definition: A place at which a service generally of interest to small craft or pleasure boats is available.

features.name: Text Placement
features.definition: The Text Placement feature is used in association with the Feature Name attribute or a light description to optimize text positioning in ECDIS.

features.name: Chart 1 Feature
features.definition: A feature which exists to support the rendering of graphics or text in order to provide additional information that cannot be encoded using other features.

attributes.name: Based On Fixed Marks
attributes.definition: A straight route (known as a recommended track, range or leading line), which comprises: a. at least two structures (usually beacons or daymarks) and/or natural features, which may carry lights and/or top-marks. The structures/features are positioned so that when observed to be in line, a vessel can follow a known bearing with safety. (Adapted from International Association of Lighthouse Authorities - IALA Aids to Navigation Guide, 1990); or b. a single structure or natural feature, which may carry lights and/or a topmark, and a specified bearing which can be followed with safety. (S-57 Edition 3.1, Appendix A Chapter 2, Page 2.72, November 2000, as amended).

attributes.name: Beacon Shape

A cardinal mark is named after the quadrant in which it is placed. The name of the cardinal mark indicates that it should be passed to the named side of the mark.

attributes.name: Category of Checkpoint

attributes.name: Category of Coastline

attributes.name: Category of Conveyor

attributes.name: Category of Crane

attributes.name: Category of Dam

attributes.name: Category of Dock

attributes.name: Category of Dolphin

attributes.name: Category of Dumping Ground

attributes.name: Category of Fence

attributes.name: Category of Ferry

attributes.name: Category of Fishing Facility
attributes.definition: Classification of fishing facility provided based on different fishing methods.

attributes.name: Category of Fog Signal

attributes.name: Category of Fortified Structure

attributes.name: Category of Gate

attributes.name: Category of Harbour Facility
attributes.definition: Classification of harbour use.

attributes.name: Category of Hulk

attributes.name: Category of Ice

attributes.name: Category of Military Practice Area
attributes.definition: Classification of area by military use.

attributes.name: Category of Mooring Area

attributes.name: Category of Navigation Line

attributes.definition: Classification of an area at sea within which there are production facilities.

attributes.name: Category of Oil Barrier
attributes.definition: Classification of barriers used to prevent the unwanted spread of oil across the sea surface.

attributes.name: Category of Opening Bridge
attributes.definition: Classification of opening structures spanning and providing passage over a gap or barrier, such as a river or roadway.

attributes.name: Category of Pile
attributes.definition: Classification of pile, driven into the earth as a foundation or support for a structure.

attributes.name: Category of Pilot Boarding Place
attributes.definition: Classification of pilot boarding method.

attributes.name: Category of Pipeline/Pipe
attributes.definition: Classification of a pipe systems use.

attributes.name: Category of Preference

attributes.name: Category of Production Area
attributes.definition: Classification of an area set aside for heavy industry.

attributes.name: Category of Pylon
attributes.definition: Classification of the pylon based on the service it is supporting.

attributes.name: Category of Radar Station
attributes.definition: Classification of radar station based on the services offered.

attributes.name: Category of Radar Transponder Beacon
attributes.definition: Classification of radar transponder beacon based on functionality.

attributes.name: Category of Radio Station
attributes.definition: Classification of radio services offered by a radio station.

attributes.name: Category of Rescue Station
attributes.definition: Classification of aid station based on life saving equipment.

attributes.name: Category of Restricted Area
attributes.definition: The official legal status of each kind of restricted area defines the kind of restriction(s), for example the restriction for a 'game reserve' may be 'entering prohibited'.

attributes.name: Category of Road
attributes.definition: Classification of a road based on size.

attributes.name: Category of Schedule
attributes.definition: The type of schedule, for instance opening, closure, etc.

attributes.name: Category of Sea Area
attributes.definition: Classification of an area based on its physical characteristics.

attributes.name: Category of Shoreline Construction
attributes.definition: Classification of shoreline construction based on use.

attributes.name: Category of Signal Station, Traffic
attributes.definition: Classification of station based on the traffic service provided.

attributes.name: Category of Signal Station, Warning
attributes.definition: Classification of station based on the warning service provided.

attributes.name: Category of Silo/Tank
attributes.definition: Classification based on the product for which a silo or tank is used.

attributes.name: Category of Slope
attributes.definition: Classification of a stretch of ground forming a natural or artificial incline.

attributes.name: Category of Small Craft Facility
attributes.definition: Classification of services and facilities for the small craft user.

attributes.name: Category of Special Purpose Mark
attributes.definition: Classification of an aid to navigation which signifies some special purpose.

attributes.name: Category of Temporal Variation
attributes.definition: An assessment of the likelihood of change over time.

Likely to Change But Significant Shoaling Not Expected

attributes.name: Category of Structure
attributes.definition: Classification of a covered or partially covered area where different use types of vessel can berth.

attributes.name: Category of Tidal Stream
attributes.definition: Classification of the alternating horizontal movement of water associated with the rise and fall of the tide caused by tide producing forces.

attributes.name: Category of Vegetation
attributes.definition: Classification of the plant life of an area or region.

attributes.name: Category of Water Turbulence
attributes.definition: Classification of an unstable sea state.

attributes.name: Category of Weed/Kelp
attributes.definition: Classification of marine vegetation of the algae class.

attributes.name: Category of Wreck
attributes.definition: Classification of a wrecked or ruined ship.

attributes.name: Category of Zone of Confidence In Data
attributes.definition: Classification of the zone of confidence in data within an area based on the positional accuracy, survey equipment and coverage.

attributes.name: Colour
attributes.definition: The property possessed by an object of producing different sensations on the eye as a result of the way it reflects or emits light.

attributes.name: Colour Pattern
attributes.definition: A regular repeated design containing more than one colour.

attributes.name: Communication Channel
attributes.definition: A channel number assigned to a specific radio frequency, frequencies or frequency band.

attributes.name: Condition
attributes.definition: The various conditions of buildings and other constructions.

attributes.name: Contact Instructions
attributes.definition: Instructions provided on how to contact a particular person, organisation or service.

attributes.name: Data Assessment
attributes.definition: The categorization of the assessment level of bathymetric data for an area.

attributes.name: Date Disused
attributes.definition: The date that an entity ceases to be used.

attributes.name: Date End
attributes.definition: The latest date on which an object (for example a buoy) will be present.

attributes.name: Date Fixed
attributes.definition: The date of an event.

attributes.name: Date Start
attributes.definition: The earliest date on which an object (for example a buoy) will be present.

attributes.name: Date Variable
attributes.definition: A day which is not fixed in the Gregorian calendar.

attributes.name: Day of Week
attributes.definition: Any one of seven days in a week.

attributes.name: Day of Week is Range
attributes.definition: A statement expressing if the days of the week identified define a range or not.

attributes.name: Default Clearance Depth
attributes.definition: The depth value determined for an underwater hazard of unknown depth, based on the depth of the surrounding area.

attributes.name: Depth Range Maximum Value
attributes.definition: The maximum (deepest) value of a depth range.

attributes.name: Depth Range Minimum Value
attributes.definition: The minimum (shoalest) value of a depth range.

attributes.name: Destination
attributes.definition: The place or general direction to which a vessel is going or directed.

attributes.name: Distance Mark Visible
attributes.definition: A statement indicating whether a distance mark is visible or not.

attributes.name: Distance Unit of Measurement
attributes.definition: A specified amount of a quantity, as of length, by comparison with which any other quantity of the same kind is measured or estimated.

attributes.name: Dredged Date
attributes.definition: The date that dredging occurred.

attributes.name: Elevation
attributes.definition: The altitude of the ground level of a feature, measured from a specified vertical datum.

attributes.name: Estimated Range of Transmission
attributes.definition: The estimated range of a non-optical electromagnetic transmission.

attributes.name: Exhibition Condition of Light
attributes.definition: The outward display of the light.

listed_values.label: Light Shown Without Change of Character

attributes.name: Exposition of Sounding
attributes.definition: Indicates the relationship of the depth of a feature to the range of depth of the surrounding depth area.

listed_values.label: Within the Range of Depth of the Surrounding Depth Area
Shoaler Than the Range of Depth of the Surrounding Depth Area
Deeper Than the Range of Depth of the Surrounding Depth Area

attributes.name: File Locator
attributes.definition: The location of a fragment of text or other information in a support file.

attributes.name: File Reference
attributes.definition: The file name of an externally referenced text file.

attributes.name: Flare Bearing
attributes.definition: The bearing about which the light flare symbol is rotated to be displayed in ECDIS.

attributes.name: Flare Stack
attributes.definition: A tall structure used for burning-off waste oil or gas.

attributes.name: Frequency Shore Station Receives
attributes.definition: The shore station receiver frequency.

attributes.name: Frequency Shore Station Transmits
attributes.definition: The shore station transmitter frequency.

attributes.name: Drawing Index
attributes.definition: A numeric value used to indicate that datasets are intended to form a seamless presentation.

attributes.name: Full Seafloor Coverage Achieved
attributes.definition: Expression stating if full seafloor coverage has been achieved in the area covered by hydrographic surveys.

attributes.name: Function
attributes.definition: A specific role that describes a feature.

attributes.name: Headline
attributes.definition: Words set at the head of a passage or page to introduce or categorize.

attributes.name: Height
attributes.definition: The value of the vertical distance to the highest point of the feature, measured from a specified vertical datum.

attributes.name: Horizontal Clearance Length
attributes.definition: The length of a feature, such as a lock or basin, which is available for safe navigation. This may, or may not, be the same as the total physical length of the feature.

attributes.name: Horizontal Clearance Value
attributes.definition: The physical horizontal clearance distance between two points on a feature, such as a bridge span, dock, gate, lock or tunnel.

attributes.name: Horizontal Clearance Width
attributes.definition: The width of a feature, such as a lock or basin, which is available for safe navigation. This may, or may not, be the same as the total physical width of the feature.

attributes.name: Horizontal Distance Uncertainty
attributes.definition: The best estimate of the horizontal accuracy of horizontal clearances and distances.

attributes.name: Horizontal Length
attributes.definition: A measurement of the longer of two linear axis.

attributes.name: Horizontal Width
attributes.definition: A measurement of the shorter of two linear axis.

attributes.name: Ice Factor
attributes.definition: The value of the maximum variation in the vertical clearance of an overhead cable due to an accumulation of ice.

attributes.name: IMO Adopted
attributes.definition: A defined maritime traffic route that has been adopted as an IMO routeing measure.

attributes.name: In Dispute
attributes.definition: A statement that expresses if an area is in a jurisdictional dispute.

attributes.name: Interoperability Identifier
attributes.definition: A common unique identifier for entities which describe a single real-world feature, and which is used to identify instances of the feature in end-user systems where the feature may be included in multiple data product types.

attributes.name: In the Water
attributes.definition: An indication if the feature is located in or over navigable water.

attributes.name: Is MRCC
attributes.definition: A statement that expresses if a Coast Guard station performs the function of a Maritime Rescue and Coordination Centre.

attributes.name: Jurisdiction
attributes.definition: The jurisdiction applicable to an administrative area.

attributes.name: Language
attributes.definition: The method of human communication, either spoken or written, consisting of the use of words in a structured and conventional way.

attributes.name: Least Depth of Detected Features Measured
attributes.definition: Expression stating if the least depth of detected features in an area was measured.

attributes.name: Lifting Capacity
attributes.definition: The specific safe lifting capacity of a feature.

attributes.name: Light Characteristic
attributes.definition: The distinct character, such as fixed, flashing, or occulting, which is given to each light to avoid confusion with neighbouring ones.

attributes.name: Light Visibility
attributes.definition: The specific visibility of a light, with respect to the light's intensity and ease of recognition.

attributes.name: Line Spacing Maximum
attributes.definition: The maximum distance between hydrographic survey lines.

attributes.name: Line Spacing Minimum
attributes.definition: The minimum distance between hydrographic survey lines.

attributes.name: Linkage
attributes.definition: Location (address) for online access using a URL/URI address or similar addressing scheme.

attributes.name: Magnetic Anomaly Value
attributes.definition: The value of the deviation from the normal magnetic variation.

attributes.name: Reference Direction
attributes.definition: A direction used as a basis for comparison of other directions.

attributes.name: Major Light
attributes.definition: A statement expressing if a light is considered to be a major light in terms of ECDIS display in a particular area.

attributes.name: Marks Navigational - System Of
attributes.definition: The system of navigational buoyage a region complies with.

listed_values.label: main European inland waterway marking system

attributes.name: Maximum Display Scale
attributes.definition: The value considered by the Data Producer to be the maximum (largest) scale at which the data is to be displayed before it can be considered to be "grossly overscaled".

attributes.name: Maximum Permitted Draught
attributes.definition: The maximum draught of a vessel permitted along a route, in a channel or dock, at a berth, or over a submerged feature.

attributes.name: Maximum Permitted Vessel Length
attributes.definition: The maximum length of a vessel permitted in a channel or dock, at a berth, or at an anchorage or mooring.

attributes.name: Measured Distance
attributes.definition: A course at sea, whose ends are indicated by ranges ashore, and whose length has been accurately measured for determining the speed of vessels.

attributes.name: Measurement Distance Maximum
attributes.definition: The maximum spacing of the principal measurement lines of a hydrographic survey.

attributes.name: Measurement Distance Minimum
attributes.definition: The minimum spacing of the principal measurement lines of a hydrographic survey.

attributes.name: Minimum Display Scale
attributes.definition: The smallest intended viewing scale for the data.

attributes.name: MMSI Code
attributes.definition: The Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI) Code is formed of a series of nine digits which are transmitted over the radio path in order to uniquely identify ship stations, ship earth stations, coast stations, coast earth stations, and group calls. These identities are formed in such a way that the identity or part thereof can be used by telephone and telex subscribers connected to the general telecommunications network principally to call ships automatically.

attributes.name: Moire Effect
attributes.definition: A short range (up to 2km) type of directional light. Sodium lighting gives a yellow background to a screen on which a vertical black line will be seen by an observer on the centre line.

attributes.name: Multiplicity Known
attributes.definition: The number of features of identical character that exist as a co-located group is or is not known.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.definition: The individual name of a feature.

attributes.name: Name of Resource
attributes.definition: Name of the online resource.

attributes.name: Name Usage
attributes.definition: Classification of the type and display level of the name of a feature in an end-user system.

attributes.name: Nationality
attributes.definition: Identifier of membership of a particular nation.

attributes.name: Nature of Construction
attributes.definition: The building's primary construction material.

attributes.name: Nature of Surface
attributes.definition: The general material which the land surface or the seabed is composed.

attributes.name: Nature of Surface - Qualifying Terms
attributes.definition: The nature of various forms of natural surface materials in terms of their size, morphology and consistency.

attributes.name: Number of Features
attributes.definition: The number of features of identical character that exist as a co-located group.

attributes.name: Opening Bridge
attributes.definition: A bridge that is closed when set for carrying road traffic and open when set to permit marine traffic to pass through the waterway it crosses. Modern opening (movable) bridges are either bascule, vertical lift or swing.

attributes.name: Orientation Uncertainty
attributes.definition: The best estimate of the accuracy of a bearing.

attributes.name: Orientation Value
attributes.definition: The angular distance measured from true north to the major axis of the feature.

attributes.name: Pictorial Representation
attributes.definition: The file name of an externally referenced picture file.

attributes.name: Pilot Movement
attributes.definition: Classification of pilot activity by arrival, departure, or change of pilot. It may also describe the place where the pilot's advice begins, ends, or is transferred to a different pilot.

attributes.name: Product
attributes.definition: The various substances which are transported, stored or exploited.

attributes.name: Quality of Horizontal Measurement
attributes.definition: The degree of reliability attributed to a position.

attributes.name: Quality of Vertical Measurement
attributes.definition: The reliability of the value of a sounding.

listed_values.label: Least Depth Unknown, Safe Clearance at Value Shown

attributes.name: Radar Band
attributes.definition: The band code character of the electromagnetic spectrum within which radar wave lengths lie.

attributes.name: Radar Conspicuous
attributes.definition: A feature which returns a strong radar echo.

attributes.name: Radius
attributes.definition: The vector extending from the centre to the periphery of a circular or spherical feature.

attributes.name: Reference Location
attributes.definition: Information relating to the point of origin for a measured distance as indicated on a distance mark.

attributes.name: Reference Tide
attributes.definition: The reference tide to which the series of tidal stream values apply.

attributes.name: Reference Tide Type
attributes.definition: The type of tide range (that is, mean spring tide, mean neap tide or mean tide) for which a set of tidal stream rates and directions apply.

attributes.name: Reference Year for Magnetic Variation
attributes.definition: The reference calendar year for magnetic variation values.

attributes.name: Regulation Citation
attributes.definition: The regulation citation for a feature.

attributes.name: Reported Date
attributes.definition: The date that the item was observed, done, or investigated.

attributes.name: Restriction
attributes.definition: The official legal statute of each kind of restricted area.

attributes.name: Scale Minimum
attributes.definition: The minimum scale at which the feature may be used for example for ECDIS presentation.

attributes.name: Scale Value Maximum
attributes.definition: The largest scale for the range of survey scale.

attributes.name: Scale Value Minimum
attributes.definition: The smallest scale for the range of survey scale.

attributes.name: Sector Bearing
attributes.definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector bearing specifies the limit of the sector.

attributes.name: Sector Arc Extension
attributes.definition: An indication that the default radius of a sector arc is to be extended by 5mm.

attributes.name: Sector Line Length
attributes.definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector line length specifies the displayed length of the line, in ground units, defining the limit of the sector.

attributes.name: Signal Duration
attributes.definition: The time occupied by a single instance of light/sound or eclipse/silence in a signal sequence.

attributes.name: Signal Frequency
attributes.definition: The frequency of a signal.

attributes.name: Signal Generation
attributes.definition: The mechanism used to generate a fog or light signal.

attributes.name: Signal Group
attributes.definition: The number of signals, the combination of signals or the morse character(s) within one period of full sequence.

attributes.name: Signal Period
attributes.definition: The time occupied by an entire cycle of intervals of light and eclipse.

attributes.name: Signal Status
attributes.definition: The indication of an element of a signal sequence being a period of light/sound or eclipse/silence.

attributes.name: Significant Features Detected
attributes.definition: A statement expressing if significant features have or have not been detected in the course of a survey.

attributes.name: Size of Features Detected
attributes.definition: The size of detected bathymetric features in an area.

attributes.name: Source
attributes.definition: The publication, document, or reference work from which information comes or is acquired.

attributes.name: Speed Limit
attributes.definition: The maximum allowed rate of travel in an area.

attributes.name: Speed Maximum
attributes.definition: Rate of motion. The terms speed and velocity are often used interchangeably, but speed is a scalar, having magnitude only, while velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction. Speed maximum is the maximum rate of travel that can occur.

attributes.name: Speed Minimum
attributes.definition: Rate of motion. The terms speed and velocity are often used interchangeably, but speed is a scalar, having magnitude only, while velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction. Speed minimum is the minimum rate of travel that can occur.

attributes.name: Speed Units
attributes.definition: The units for description of speed.

attributes.name: Station Name
attributes.definition: The name of the reference tide station with reference water level for tidal stream panel observations.

attributes.name: Station Number
attributes.definition: The identification number of the reference tide station with reference water level for tidal stream panel observations.

attributes.name: Status
attributes.definition: The condition of an object at a given instant in time.

attributes.name: Stream Depth
attributes.definition: The depth below the sea surface to which the tidal stream data refers relative to the sounding datum.

attributes.name: Surrounding Depth
attributes.definition: The depth value determined for seabed around an underwater hazard, based on the depth of the surrounding area.

attributes.name: Survey Authority
attributes.definition: The authority which was responsible for the survey.

attributes.name: Survey Type
attributes.definition: Classification of the different survey types.

attributes.name: Update Number
attributes.definition: Update number of the ENC being referenced.

attributes.name: Update Type
attributes.definition: An action performed when the contents of a dataset are changed.

attributes.name: Swept Date
attributes.definition: The date that the area was swept by a survey.

attributes.name: Technique of Vertical Measurement
attributes.definition: Survey method used to obtain depth information.

attributes.name: Telecommunication Identifier
attributes.definition: An identifier, such as words, numbers, letters, symbols, or any combination of those used to establish a contact to a particular person, organisation or service.

attributes.name: Telecommunication Service
attributes.definition: Classification of methods of communication over a distance by electrical, electronic, or electromagnetic means.

attributes.name: Text
attributes.definition: A non-formatted digital text string.

attributes.name: Text Offset Bearing
attributes.definition: The angular distance measured from true north that text associated with a feature is positioned from the feature in an end-user system.

attributes.name: Text Offset Distance
attributes.definition: The distance that text associated with a feature is positioned from the feature in an end-user system.

attributes.name: Text Rotation
attributes.definition: A statement that expresses if text associated with a feature is to be rotated in the ECDIS display or not.

attributes.name: Text Type
attributes.definition: The attribute from which a text string is derived.

attributes.name: Time of Day End
attributes.definition: The time corresponding to the end of an active period.

attributes.name: Time of Day Start
attributes.definition: The time corresponding to the start of an active period.

attributes.name: Time Relative to Tide
attributes.definition: The time difference relative to the reference tide.

attributes.name: Topmark/Daymark Shape
attributes.definition: The shape a topmark or daymark exhibits.

listed_values.label: Two Upright Crosses (One Over the Other)
Triangle Pointing Up Over a Circle
Circle Over a Triangle Pointing Up

attributes.name: Traffic Flow
attributes.definition: Direction of vessels passing a reference point.

attributes.name: Uncertainty Fixed
attributes.definition: The best estimate of the fixed horizontal or vertical accuracy component for positions, depths, heights, vertical distances and vertical clearances.

attributes.name: Uncertainty Variable Factor
attributes.definition: The factor to be applied to the variable component of an uncertainty equation so as to provide the best estimate of the variable horizontal or vertical accuracy component for positions, depths, heights, vertical distances and vertical clearances.

attributes.name: Underlying Layer
attributes.definition: The position of the seabed type within the layers of the seabed.

attributes.name: Value of Annual Change in Magnetic Variation
attributes.definition: The annual change in magnetic variation values.

attributes.name: Value of Depth Contour
attributes.definition: The depth of a sea bottom contour.

attributes.name: Value of Magnetic Variation
attributes.definition: The angle between the magnetic and geographical meridians at any place, expressed in degrees east or west to indicate the direction of magnetic north from true north.

attributes.name: Value of Maximum Range
attributes.definition: The extreme distance at which a feature can be seen or a signal detected.

attributes.name: Value of Nominal Range
attributes.definition: The luminous range of a light in a homogenous atmosphere in which the meteorological visibility is 10 sea miles.

attributes.name: Value of Sounding
attributes.definition: The value of the measurement of a sounding relative to the chart datum.

attributes.name: Vertical Clearance Unlimited
attributes.definition: A statement that expresses if the vertical clearance for a feature in the open position, such as a bridge span, is unlimited.

attributes.name: Vertical Clearance Value
attributes.definition: The vertical clearance measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

attributes.name: Vertical Datum
attributes.definition: The reference level used for expressing the vertical measurements of points on the earth's surface. Also called datum level, reference plane, levelling datum, datum for sounding reduction, datum for heights.

attributes.name: Vertical Length
attributes.definition: The total vertical length of a feature.

attributes.name: Vessel Class
attributes.definition: The classification of a vessel, normally as defined by length or gross tonnage.

attributes.name: Virtual AIS Aid to Navigation Type
attributes.definition: A purpose of a virtual AIS Aid to Navigation.

attributes.name: Visitors Mooring
attributes.definition: A mooring set aside for the use of visiting vessels.

attributes.name: Visual Prominence
attributes.definition: The extent to which a feature, either natural or artificial, is visible from seaward.

attributes.name: Water Level Effect
attributes.definition: The effect of the surrounding water on an object.

attributes.name: Waterway Distance
attributes.definition: The length of the space between two points along a waterway.

attributes.name: Wave Length Value
attributes.definition: The distance between two successive peaks (or other points of identical phase) on an electromagnetic wave.

attributes.name: Category of Cargo
attributes.definition: Classification of the different types of cargo that a ship may be carrying.

attributes.name: Minimum Berth Depth
attributes.definition: The least depth of the body of water at the berth or in a berth pocket adjacent to the berth.

attributes.name: Optimum Display Scale
attributes.definition: The largest intended viewing scale for the data.

attributes.name: Drawing Instruction
attributes.definition: Text describing one or more graphic elements that must be rendered in an end-user system.

attributes.name: Directional Character
attributes.definition: A directional light is a light illuminating a sector of very narrow angle and intended to mark a direction to follow.

attributes.name: Feature Name
attributes.definition: Provides the name of an entity, defines the national language of the name, and provides the option to display the name at various system display settings.

attributes.name: Features Detected
attributes.definition: The uniform assessment of detected features.

attributes.name: Fixed Date Range
attributes.definition: An active period of a single fixed event or occurrence, as the date range between discrete start and end dates.

attributes.name: Frequency Pair
attributes.definition: A pair of frequencies for transmitting and receiving radio signals. The shore station transmits and receives on the frequencies indicated.

attributes.name: Horizontal Clearance Fixed
attributes.definition: The horizontal clearance measured between two points for a fixed span.

attributes.name: Horizontal Clearance Open
attributes.definition: The horizontal clearance measured between two points for an opening span.

attributes.name: Horizontal Position Uncertainty
attributes.definition: The best estimate of the accuracy of a position.

attributes.name: Information
attributes.definition: Textual information about the feature. The information may be provided as a string of text or as a file name of a single external text file that contains the text.

attributes.name: Light Sector
attributes.definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference.

attributes.name: Measured Distance Value
attributes.definition: The distance value indicated on a distance mark, or the distance between two measured distance marks.

attributes.name: Multiplicity of Features
attributes.definition: The number of features of identical character that exist as a co-located group.

attributes.name: Online Resource
attributes.definition: Information about online sources from which a resource or data can be obtained.

attributes.name: Orientation
attributes.definition: The angular distance measured from true north to the major axis of the feature.

attributes.name: Periodic Date Range
attributes.definition: The active period of a recurring event or occurrence.

attributes.name: Radar Wave Length
attributes.definition: The distance between two successive peaks (or other points of identical phase) on an electromagnetic wave in the radar band of the electromagnetic spectrum.

attributes.name: Rhythm of Light
attributes.definition: The sequence of times occupied by intervals of light/sound and eclipse/silence for all light characteristics or sound signals.

attributes.name: Schedule by Day of Week
attributes.definition: The nature and timings of a daily schedule by days of the week.

attributes.name: Sector Characteristics
attributes.definition: Describes the characteristics of a light sector.

attributes.name: Sector Information
attributes.definition: Additional textual information about a light sector.

attributes.name: Sector Limit
attributes.definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. The sector limit specifies the limits of the sector In a clockwise direction around the central feature (for example a light).

attributes.name: Sector Limit One
attributes.definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector limit one specifies the first limit of the sector. The order of sector limit one and sector limit two is clockwise around the central feature (for example a light).

attributes.name: Sector Limit Two
attributes.definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector limit two specifies the second limit of the sector. The order of sector limit one and sector limit two is clockwise around the central feature (for example a light).

attributes.name: Shape Information
attributes.definition: Textual information about the shape of a non-standard topmark.

attributes.name: Signal Sequence
attributes.definition: The sequence of times occupied by intervals of light/sound and eclipse/silence for all “light characteristics” or sound signals.

attributes.name: Spatial Accuracy
attributes.definition: Provides an indication of the vertical and horizontal positional uncertainty of bathymetric data, optionally within a specified date range.

attributes.name: Speed
attributes.definition: Rate of motion. The terms speed and velocity are often used interchangeably, but speed is a scalar, having magnitude only, while velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.

attributes.name: Surface Characteristics
attributes.definition: The general nature of the material of which the land surface or the seabed is composed.

attributes.name: Survey Date Range
attributes.definition: The complex attribute describes the period of the hydrographic survey, as the time between its sub-attributes.

attributes.name: Telecommunications
attributes.definition: A means or channel of communicating at a distance by electrical or electromagnetic means such as telegraphy, telephony, or broadcasting.

attributes.name: Tidal Stream Panel Values
attributes.definition: The direction of the flow and the tidal current rate from 6 hours before to 6 hours after high water (HW) or low water (LW) at the reference tide station, at hourly or sub-hourly intervals.

attributes.name: Tidal Stream Value
attributes.definition: A measurement of the direction and speed of a tidal stream at a given time relative to the reference tide.

attributes.name: Time Intervals by Day of Week
attributes.definition: The regular weekly operation times of a service or schedule.

attributes.name: Topmark
attributes.definition: A characteristic shape secured at the top of a buoy or beacon to aid in its identification.

attributes.name: Value of Local Magnetic Anomaly
attributes.definition: The value of the deviation from the normal magnetic variation and where required its direction.

attributes.name: Vertical Clearance Closed
attributes.definition: The vertical clearance of a feature in closed condition (for example a closed lifting bridge) measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

attributes.name: Vertical Clearance Fixed
attributes.definition: The vertical clearance measured from the horizontal plane towards a fixed (non-opening) feature overhead.

attributes.name: Vertical Clearance Open
attributes.definition: The vertical clearance of a feature in opened condition (for example an open lifting bridge) measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

attributes.name: Vertical Clearance Safe
attributes.definition: The safe vertical clearance of a feature measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

attributes.name: Vertical Uncertainty
attributes.definition: The best estimate of the vertical accuracy of depths, heights, vertical distances and vertical clearances.

attributes.name: Vessel Speed Limit
attributes.definition: The maximum allowed rate of travel for a vessel in an area in knots.

attributes.name: Zone of Confidence
attributes.definition: The overall indication of the quality of bathymetric data within an area based on the positional accuracy, survey equipment and coverage; optionally within a specified data range.
